predecessors.name: Union of Burma (Myanmar)
predecessors.text: Kachin State less its major towns and railway corridor: 'Aside from its major towns and railway corridor, KIO/A-controlled areas in Kachin State remained virtually independent ... from the mid-1960s…

ledger.x: 1961: the Kachin Independence Army is formed on 5 February: 'a year later on 5 February 1961, the KIO's 100-strong private army was reorganised into the Kachin Independence Army'.

1962: after the March coup Kachin soldiers 'defected from the military' and joined the existing insurgents (Internal conflict page); the KIO page: areas in Kachin State 'remained virtually independent' from the mid-1960s.
1994: a ceasefire is brokered between the KIO/A and the government ('until a ceasefire was brokered between the two opposing sides in 1994'); the exact date is not on the page.
2005: 'the KIO moved its headquarters from Pajau to Laiza'.
2011: the ceasefire breaks on 9 June when 'the Tatmadaw resumed operations against the KIA'.
2024-09: the KIO takes Chipwi and Panwa.

wars.name: Kachin conflict (1961-1994)
wars.outcome: KIO/A areas remained 'virtually independent' until the 1994 ceasefire.

wars.name: Kachin conflict (2011-)
wars.outcome: Fighting resumed on 9 June 2011; after the 2021 coup the KIA seized military bases, in 2024 the KIO took Panwa and Chipwe (Chipwi on the evening of 30 September 2024) and in December 2024 the KIA launched an operation on Bhamo with no capture reported.

certainty.note: An insurgent area with no published boundary; Kachin State is a claim and an upper bound.
